spec_url: https://www.sec.gov/files/absxml-31.zip (EDGAR ABS XML Technical Specification v3.1, listed at https://www.sec.gov/submit-filings/technical-specifications); code meanings read from the annotations in eis_ABS_AutoLoanAssetData.xsd (the copy the Ally session unpacked in data/raw/ally/spec_absxml31/, read only). Capital One's own field narratives are in each pool filing's EX-103 (Asset Related Document), e.g. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2089663/000119312525247047/copart251ex103_1022-1407lp.xml
notes: Only two Capital One Prime Auto Receivables Trust deals were filed between Jan 2024 and Feb 28 2026, so this issuer has two Parquets, not three. The depositor Capital One Auto Receivables LLC (CIK 0001133438) filing list (data.sec.gov submissions JSON, read Nov 15 2026) shows prime pool filings for 2023-1 (2023-02-07), 2023-2 (2023-09-26), 2024-1 (2024-11-13), 2025-1 (2025-10-22) and 2026-1 (2026-09-02), and EDGAR full-text search for 424H/424B5 naming the trust (Oct 2023 - Mar 2026) returned only 2023-2, 2024-1 and 2025-1. Brief windows: Jan-Jun 2024 has no deal, nearest in range is 2024-1; Jan-Jun 2025 has no deal, nearest in range is again 2024-1 (49 days before the window vs 114 days after for 2025-1); Oct 2025 - Feb 2026 is 2025-1. 2023-2 (filed Sep 2023) and 2026-1 (Sep 2026, already parsed by the main session in data/raw/carmax_forward/) are outside the allowed range and were not used.

Each Parquet equals the pool in the final prospectus: row counts equal the 424B5 receivable counts (2024-1: 49,532; 2025-1: 72,469), the sum of reportingPeriodActualEndBalanceAmount equals the 424B5 aggregate principal balance to the cent ($1,116,124,822.45; $1,456,229,893.76), every row's reporting period ends on the cut-off date (09-30-2024; 09-30-2025), and the balance-weighted new-vehicle share equals the 424B5 (28.57%; 26.46%, which also confirms vehicleNewUsedCode 1 = New).

2025-1 has two pool files filed 2025-10-22, one per deal size in the 424H: 'sp' (accession 0001193125-25-246960, the Base Transaction: $1,092,162,854.95, 54,436 receivables) and 'lp' (accession 0001193125-25-247047, the Upsize Transaction: $1,456,229,893.76, 72,469 receivables). The 424B5 uses the Upsize figures, so the lp file is parsed; the sp file was not downloaded. 2024-1 has a single pool file.

Pools are seasoned and narrow: 2024-1 loans were originated 2023-03 to 2024-02 and 2025-1 loans 2024-03 to 2025-02 (the cut-off dates are 7 months after the newest origination). The newest Capital One loan in these files is from Feb 2025; Capital One loans originated Mar 2025 - Jan 2026 are only in the 2026-1 pool (filed Sep 2026).

credit_score_type is 'FICO' for every row. Capital One's EX-103 item 3(e)(1): a FICO score obtained by CONA at origination from a national consumer credit reporting company (the version, e.g. FICO Auto vs classic FICO, is not stated). Item 3(e)(2): with more than one obligor, CONA uses one obligor's score or an average, by a proprietary method. Every score is numeric; ranges are 700-885 (2024-1) and 700-884 (2025-1), equal to the 424B5 minimum and maximum, so the pools are prime-only (700+). Scores above 850 are kept as written (943 rows in 2024-1, 1,782 in 2025-1).

pti_pct is paymentToIncomePercentage AS WRITTEN, not x100: Capital One writes it already in percent (median 5.53 / 4.95, max 20.94 / 21.25), while CarMax writes fractions. apr_pct is originalInterestRatePercentage x100 as in CONTRACT (the file writes 0.0599 for 5.99%), rounded to 6 decimals. (The main session's data/raw/carmax_forward/parquet/capone_2026-1.parquet was made with the unmodified CarMax parser, so its pti_pct is x100 too large, median 498.)

Code meanings (EDGAR spec XSD): subvented 0 = No (every row; Capital One's EX-103 says no receivable has rate subvention and manufacturer cash rebates are not treated as subvention); new_used_code 1 = New, 2 = Used; interest_rate_type_code 1 = Fixed (every row); vehicle_type_code 1 Car, 2 Truck, 3 SUV, 98 Other (EX-103: not a car, truck, SUV or motorcycle, e.g. minivans or vans); vehicle_value_source_code 1 = Invoice Price, 98 = Other, which Capital One's EX-103 defines as a third-party valuation guide such as Kelley Blue Book or NADA (CarMax's 98 means the sales price, so vehicle_value is not the same quantity across issuers); income_verification_code 2 = stated, not verified, 3 = verified (EX-103: Capital One reports 3 for any verified income because it cannot tell level 3 from 4 or 5); employment_verification_code 2 = stated, not verified, 3 = level 3 verified.

Other EX-103 items that matter for the model: originationDate is the funding date; originalLoanTerm is months from origination to original maturity, rounded up, so it can exceed the number of payments (the 424B5 range is 18-75 payments); originalInterestRatePercentage is the contract rate and ignores later discretionary decreases; vehicleManufacturerName is truncated to 8 characters and vehicleModelName to 12; obligorGeographicLocation is the current mailing state at the cut-off date, not at origination; all receivables were originated by Capital One, N.A. through motor vehicle dealers (424B5: retail installment sale contracts 'purchased and originated through motor vehicle dealers') and none was an underwriting exception (EX-103 item 3(c)(11)).

Download method: every sec.gov request went through data/raw/capone/sec_get.py with the User-Agent from CLAUDE.md (read from that file at run time, so the contact address is not in any committed file), one at a time with a 1 s sleep before each; all requests are in data/raw/capone/sec_requests.log (git-ignored). Each XML's size equals EDGAR's directory listing (190,447,160 and 278,614,189 bytes).
couldnt_confirm: Which FICO model Capital One reports (classic FICO 8 vs FICO Auto Score): neither the EX-103 nor the 424B5 text searched names the version. Scores above 850 (max 885) cannot occur on the classic 300-850 FICO scale, even averaged across co-obligors, which points to an auto-industry FICO version (250-900 scale), but the filings do not say so. Looked in both EX-103 files and both 424B5s.
The 2025-1 'sp' pool file was not downloaded or parsed; its count and balance come from the 424H (accession 0001193125-25-248706), not from the XML.

Whether Capital One priced any other prime retail auto-loan trust (outside the 'Capital One Prime Auto Receivables Trust' name) in Jan 2024 - Feb 2026 was not searched beyond the depositor's filing list.
